newsitem.title: UK: North Sea Brent spot and paper market weakening.
newsitem.headline: North Sea Brent spot and paper market weakening.

text.p: Spot and paper North Sea Brent crude weakened further on Wednesday afternoon with little fresh demand seen into early March and talk of a developing overhang of February barrels.

Traders said talk that one U.S. trade house had liquidated a position involving four Brent cargoes loading Feb 22 against the simultaneous purchase of a similar amount of Colombian Cusiana could mean the prompt Brent market is four cargoes longer than it expected against a background of slack demand.
This combined with a Feb 26-28 Brent cargo additional to the February programme added to the market's already bearish tone.
The Feb 26-28 Brent traded at March Brent +5 cents -- down from a +12 cent deal on Tuesday for a Feb 22-24 loader.
Equity holders said the cargo was additional to the original programme, and it was heard destined for Eastern Europe.
Few buyers were seen for the remaining three Feb cargoes and one seller asked March +5 -- down from an early offer at +15.
"There are no buyers and even the (transatlantic arbitrage) is closed." one trader said, "At Least in the past we had the pretence of an arb, but there's nothing there this time."
Brent equity holders expected the March loading programme, not expected to hold many surprises, to be released on Thursday.
"It'll just be up a bit because of the longer month," one equity holder said.
In the Med, Russian Urals was steady around -90 cents cif Genoa as the impact of loading delays at Novorossiisk balanced slack spot demand from refiners, traders said.
The Black Sea port remained shut because of high winds and swell after reopening for only three hours on Tuesday.

Nigerian crudes looked more stable after slipping last week. Traders said Bonny Light was drawing support from sales into the Far East, but Forcados was still under pressure from unsold barrels in the first decade of March.
